<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line), actionUrl (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line), actionUrl (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via DashboardHeaderActionSchema (symbol, a top-level const), actionUrl (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line), actionUrl (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line), actionUrl (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget; a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8ac777fba670805e353cbffaffe2458fcbbc2b5` — the merge of head `e9ff53c82db9703a18425a4fb2e36fb630ee4a7b` into base `21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8ac777fba670805e353cbffaffe2458fcbbc2b5 && git checkout d8ac777fba670805e353cbffaffe2458fcbbc2b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96 e9ff53c82db9703a18425a4fb2e36fb630ee4a7b && git checkout -B drift-repro 21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96 && git merge --no-ff e9ff53c82db9703a18425a4fb2e36fb630ee4a7b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 21c86444ec6e1afb3f3d6e608443fcaae6a10f96` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed59283ff50ef870d35db074c121c699bf21cf41`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract-review subagent of `domain:spec` seat 1 (seat post #6017, account `os-warren`), rendered 2026-10-12T22:16Z. Read-only. Inputs: card #23077 (body and all five comments: triage `6129646171` and `6130597965`, claim `6131231192`, dev report `6133317304`, the seat's acceptance `6133420836`); ruling A+ on objectstack-ai/objectui#12191 (comment `6121792024`) with `packages/spec/src/ui/navigation-target.ts` at `main`; PR #23101's body, file list (13 files, +559 / −21 = 580 changed lines) and net diff against `main`; the check-runs on this head; and the two issues the seat filed from the report, objectstack-ai/objectui#12275 and #23103. Producer sweeps were read at objectstack `origin/main` `d0f1c5bfb977` and objectui at the pin `7578323a544e` (`.objectui-sha`). Nothing was built, run or re-run. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **One grammar, three doors — right.** Each new refinement calls `navigationTargetRefusal` and carries no scheme literal of its own: `refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget` in `component.zod.ts`, `refuseUnopenableHeaderActionUrl` in `dashboard.zod.ts`, `refuseUnopenableOnSuccessNavigate` in `action.zod.ts`. The only literals are the executor value `'url'` and the refusal subjects. No door pre-judges a value that opens with `${`; the deferral stays inside the predicate, so `${result.redirectUrl}` is admitted by the predicate's own rule, and that is pinned. `navigation-target.ts` is still reached by relative import only, as its header requires. No export is added, removed or renamed (the three functions and `HEADER_ACTION_URL_SUBJECT` are module-private), so the published type surface is unchanged.

2. **The page action rows (`ActionButtonPropsSchema`, `ActionIconPropsSchema`, the `action:group` and `action:menu` member builders) — right.** Narrowed only when the executor key reads `'url'` and `target` is a string; a non-url executor, no executor and no `target` are untouched, all three pinned. A page's `properties` bag is outside the stack parse, so the door `os validate` judges is the props gate, which parses against the same `ComponentPropsMap` rows (pinned in `packages/lint` with no lint code change). The finding is a `component-props-invalid` warning, that gate's one tier; the card puts the error upgrade out of scope, and the changeset says the gate "reports" it rather than refuses it, which is the honest claim. The pinned sibling: objectui at `7578323a544e` consumes these rows through `stripImportedDefaults`, whose walker clones each node by patching `_zod.def` and never rebuilds with `z.object(shape)`, precisely so `def.checks` survive; read, not executed. The Console Pin Gate is skipped on `pull_request` by design (`ci.yml`, full battery only) and judges this after the merge.

3. **`DashboardHeaderActionSchema.actionUrl` when `actionType` is `'url'` — right.** Refused at `actionUrl`; the five other types are untouched and pinned; the stack-parse path `dashboards.0.header.actions.0.actionUrl` and `defineStack` are pinned.

4. **An omitted `actionType` judged as the url route — right; within the card and within the ruling; not an escalation.** The card's own measured defect names this spelling ("with `actionType: 'url'` or with it omitted") and states the renderer's default ("`DashboardRenderer` defaults an omitted `actionType` to `'url'`"); the triage direction and the claim name `DashboardHeaderActionSchema.actionUrl` unscoped. The ruling fixes the set and the principle (stated once in the contract, the runtime fulfils exactly that); which spellings of this door are a url target is the card's finding, and the diff follows the only two readers that give the omission a meaning, both read by me: objectui `headerActionDefs` at the pin (`type: actionType || 'url'`, line 459) and lint `validateDashboardActionRefs` ("a missing actionType is treated as a 'url' navigation", line 285). The diff materialises no default (no `.default('url')`; an admitted value parses byte-identically, pinned), requires nothing new, and refuses nothing that navigates today: the renderer's click handler drops an omitted type with a console warning (pin line 1221), so the omitted-type button is dead on every value before and after. Had the diff required `actionType` or materialised a default, that would have gone beyond the card; it does neither. The handler's own departure from its `headerActionDefs` reading is the runtime's, carried by objectui#12275.

5. **`ActionSchema.onSuccess.navigate` — right.** Judged on every value; `tasks/${result.id}` is refused because the runner refuses `tasks/42` after interpolation; `/apps/crm/tasks/${result.id}`, an `https://` URL and `${result.redirectUrl}` are pinned admitted. The refinement sits on the `onSuccess` object itself, so every embedding of `ActionSchema` gets it (the stack's `actions[]` and the object-level `actions`, which the baseline's new sites enumerate); `InlineActionSchema` picks no `onSuccess`, so there is no inline door to miss. An empty `navigate` is refused like any other value, matching the runner's `readOnSuccessNavigation`, which drops `''` and performs no hop (pin line 2535).

6. **The empty string at all three doors — right.** The predicate judges `''` as a bare relative and refuses it; the runtime does nothing with one anywhere (the header click handler warns on a falsy `actionUrl`, `readOnSuccessNavigation` drops it, `executeUrl` answers "No URL provided"). The changeset's FROM → TO table names the case. No producer writes one: objectui at the pin writes no `actionUrl: ''`, and the `DashboardWithConfig` seeding its CHANGELOG records was on the retired widget key and is gone.

7. **Producers — none refused.** Objectstack at `d0f1c5bfb977`: the only url header actions outside tests are docs `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` and the skill `objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md`, both `/reports/forecast`; the examples declare no dashboard header at all; the only `onSuccess.navigate` is the documented `/apps/crm/tasks/${result.id}`; no url-executor page action row exists outside tests (every `type: 'url'` hit is a registered action, already closed by #23076, or a navigation item). Objectui at `7578323a544e`: no `actionType: 'url'` producer, no header-action literal, no `navigate:` literal outside tests; `useHomeInbox`'s `actionUrl` is the inbox message key, a different shape. The only refused literals anywhere are tests that exercise the refusal.

8. **The `describe` text, the TSDoc and the three regenerated reference pages — right.** Each key now states the set it enforces; `content/docs/references/**` is generated output, not hand-edited, and `check:docs` is what the dev's `check:generated` named.

9. **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, +21 sites, totals 231 / 734 — right and consistent.** Counted in the diff: 12 `onSuccess` positions and 5 `header.actions.element` positions across 13 existing entries (17), plus 4 new root entries (`ui/ActionButtonProps`, `ui/ActionIconProps`, `ui/DashboardHeader`, `ui/DashboardHeaderAction`). The member-level row refinement lands on the existing `actions.element` site of `ui/ActionGroupProps` and `ui/ActionMenuProps`, so no new site there. No site is removed, which is the ledger's shrink-only direction; `build-schemas` enforces it and `Build Core` is green.

10. **Check-runs on this head, as read at this write:** 40 total; 34 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, each path- or event-skipped by design), 1 `in_progress` (Test Core 3/6), 0 failures. Green: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and its four shards, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE`), Spec property liveness, every Lint shard, and Test Core shards 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. The queue's own "every check green" condition waits on the last shard; that is the seat's pre-queue read, not this record's.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/23077-url-target-doors-scheme-set.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and the marker `adr-0087: registered` naming the three D3 ids. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the claim declared it; all three agree. The arm is correct: the diff removes nothing an author can write and adds no accepted shape, so it is not a widening, and it narrows three accept sets, which is BREAKING under the declaration grammar. The ruling comment estimated `Clause-②: yes` for the sibling #23010 before any claim; #23010 landed as `no (narrowing)` and this card's triage said `no`; the contract-tier review is owed on the path limb either way, and the `(narrowing)` arm is the signal `check-adr-0087-registration` reads, so nothing turns on that wording.
- The level: `minor` with the banner is what ADR-0087's ratified launch-window section states for a pre-GA metadata-facing break (the level is not the carrier of breaking-ness during the window; the banner and the disposition entry are), and `check-changeset-no-major` enforces it. It is the form the sibling #23010 changeset landed in.
- The migration: the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are present; each D3 entry states its `⛔ NOT mechanically convertible` judgment; the three entries (`18.ui-page-action-row-url-target-scheme-set-closed`, `18.ui-dashboard-header-action-url-scheme-set-closed`, `18.ui-action-on-success-navigate-scheme-set-closed`) carry every `SemanticMigration` field (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`) in the shape of the landed `18.ui-action-url-target-scheme-set-closed.ts`, and no `conversionIds`, correctly, since no D2 conversion is attached. The registry is gitignored and regenerated, so nothing else was owed. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- It matches what the diff publishes: three new refinements on published schemas reachable from the `ui` barrel, changed description strings, no export change.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. The dev's mechanism readings A1 (the `onSuccess.navigate` line corrected to `action.zod.ts:1785`), A2 (red at base shown through three one-time ablations, each restored to HEAD) and A4 (the `${` deferral pinned) are accepted as read; A3 is judged in ① item 4. The six out-of-scope findings, each answered:

1. **objectui `DashboardRenderer`'s header click handler keeps its own url grammar and bypasses the `ActionRunner`** (a protocol-relative `//host` is assigned, `mailto:` throws at `pushState`, a bare relative is admitted). Answered; carried by objectstack-ai/objectui#12275, which I read: it asks for the click to go through the runner with no scheme list of its own, and for an omitted `actionType` to mean `'url'` at the click, with pins. The contract door is right to match `navigationTargetRefusal` and the runner's `classifyNavigationTarget` rather than this handler; a door written to the handler would be the second grammar the ruling forbids. Stated plainly: until #12275 lands, a `mailto:` header action parses clean and throws at the dashboard click, the ruling's own dead-button class, and the omitted-type button stays dead. That is the runtime half, objectui's under ruling A+, and not a condition of this verdict.
2. **The omitted-type dead button.** Folded into objectui#12275; same handler, same fix. Answered.
3. **The rows' `onSuccess` is `z.unknown()`**: `onSuccess: { navigate: 'javascript:…' }` on an `action:button` parses clean and the props gate answers 0 findings. Answered; carried by #23103, which I read. A fourth door, outside this card's three; it needs a contract choice for the rows' `onSuccess` shape, a claim of its own and not a rider here.
4. **`actionType: 'navigation'` on a page action row** reaches `executeNavigation`, an alias of `url`, with `target` unjudged. Answered as a residual, not a blocker; a carrier is owed. The rows' executor key is a free `z.string()`, so the alias spelling admits what the click refuses (`executeNavigation` to `navigateTo` to `classifyNavigationTarget`, pin lines 1150, 2221 and 1964). The card and the claim scope the rows to `'url'`, and no producer writes it, so it is outside this PR. Because it is a measured contract-admits-what-the-runtime-refuses shape, it belongs on #23103's family thread or a finding of its own rather than in Acceptance notes alone. The seat's call; it does not change this verdict.
5. **Three `validate-dashboard-action-refs.test.ts` fixtures now pin raw objects the stack parse refuses first.** Answered. They feed the lint rule directly and pin that rule's own reading (`actionType ?? 'url'`; a protocol-relative value treated as external and skipped); they remain valid unit pins and no longer describe a reachable stack. Test hygiene, not a contract surface.
6. **`action.form.ts`'s help text ("A relative value is an in-app route") and the props gate's generic `component-props-invalid` sentence read loosely.** Answered as drift. The help text is Studio copy under `packages/spec/src/ui/` and now points toward a bare relative value the parse refuses; the parse's own message carries the correct prescription, so an author is not left without the fix. Owed on the next edit, as the seat recorded; not a condition of this verdict.

File surface beyond the claim's literal list: the baseline ledger (hand-edited by design, no `gen:` script), the three D3 entries (owed by `check-adr-0087-registration` once the changeset carries a FROM → TO prescription) and the three regenerated reference pages. Each is a consequence the claim's "generated artifacts `check:generated` names" and the changeset's registration imply, and each is declared in the PR body and the report. No governed path is touched (the file list has no `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`), so this record serves the published-schema face and the `(narrowing)` declaration, not Tier S.
